recipe.title: Panforte
recipe.notes: This is a recipe from Alexandra Campbell's mum, Raewyn

method.s: Roughly chop almonds, spread in a shallow baking tray and put in a low oven to dry and just faintly colour.
Roast hazelnuts in the oven at 160 degrees until just starting to darken, then tip onto a clean tea towel and rub vigorously to remove skins.
Grease a round, shallow sponge tin (20 cm diameter). Line base and sides with baking paper. Do not grease the paper.
Chop all the nuts coarsely. Mix cooled nuts, ginger, cherries and peel.
Sift together the flour, cocoa and cinnamon. Add to the nuts and fruit and mix.
Break chocolate into squares and melt over hot water or in the microwave.

In a saucepan, stir sugar, honey and water over a low heat to completely dissolve the sugar. Wash down the sides of the pan with a pastry brush to ensure all of the sugar dissolves. Bring to the boil and boil to the soft-ball stage (that is, a little mixture when dropped in a cup of cold water can be gathered in the fingers in a loose ball). Remove from the heat immediately.

Now work quickly and have a very firm scraper to hand. Mix the syrup and the melted chocolate into the fruit and nut mix. Spread the mixture in the lined tin, and use the back of a wet spoon to smooth the top. The mixture will be quite stiff.
Bake for 35 minutes. Cool in the tin.
When cool, remove the paper, and wrap in waxed paper and then foil, sealing well. Store in a cool place until Christmas. The panforte will soften slightly with storage.
